title: Local perfect charts for one universal direct-image rank condition
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat, proper and locally of finite presentation, with universally invertible structure-sheaf adjunction unit [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Let $E,F$ be finite locally free modules on $X$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Use derived categories of the scheme module categories and their open over-sites in one universe [def-pc-derived-category]. For every $s\in S$ there exist an open neighbourhood $U$, a perfect object $K$ on $U$ [def-pc-perfect-complex], $b\in\mathbf Z$, and $r\in\mathbf N$ such that $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every module $M$ when $i<0$ or $b<i$ [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. For every $g:T\to U$, the single-rank predicate $R_1(f,E,F,g\circ\iota_U)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-single-rank-match] holds if and only if, for every $h:T'\to T$, $H^0(L(g\circ h)^*K)$ is finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. This statement constructs the local complex and comparison, not a representing subscheme.

proof.text: Apply the unit on residue-field base changes: global functions are the residue field. Fibres are nonempty and connected (a decomposition gives a nontrivial idempotent). The rank of E is constant on each fibre. Apply the clopen fixed-fibre-rank theorem and take the stratum through s. Tensor pullback preserves rank, so E has this same rank r after every further base change on this stratum.

Finite local freeness makes F finitely presented and flat relative to the stratum. Apply perfect derived direct image and arbitrary base change. Restrict to a neighbourhood of s with a finite Tor upper bound b. Every base change is the derived direct image of a sheaf in degree zero, so has no negative cohomology; by the local strictly perfect model and the fibre criterion, its Tor amplitude starts at zero. This gives K and the displayed all-module vanishing.

The derived base change comparison and degree-zero right-derived direct image identify H^0 of each derived pullback with the ordinary direct image of the tensor pullback of F. In a local witness for R_1, compare the rank of E on any nonempty fibre with the fixed r, so the witness rank equals r. Local rank-r witnesses on an open cover of each further test give global rank-r finite local freeness. Conversely, global rank-r freeness gives the local witness (the whole test scheme), and the reference E already has rank r. This proves both implications, including empty tests and r=0.
